Frank Norris, The Pit.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/frank-norris/the-pit

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Frank Norris, the author, died 1902 (Wikidata Q712746, P570 = 1902-10-25).

First publication of the text used: 1903 (SE colophon: 'The Pit was published in 1903 by Frank Norris.'; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pit_(Norris_novel) lists the United States as the country and Doubleday, Page & Co. as the publisher; a shorter version ran in the Saturday Evening Post, a United States magazine, from September 1902 to January 1903, before the book).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1903, before 1931. A work published in 1903 entered the United States public domain on 1 January 1999. Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published there, so the US rule settles the origin whatever the death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
